newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, U.S. still to discuss wheat import issue.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, U.S. still to discuss wheat import issue.

text.p: A meeting last week of Brazilian and U.S. officials to discuss phytosanitary issues did not include talks on changes which would facilitate imports of U.S. wheat, a Brazilian Agriculture Ministry official said.
"There was a decision that this issue would be only discussed at two meetings - one this month in North Carolina in the U.S. and the other in Passo Fundo in Brazil in October," the official said.

U.S. wheat exports to Brazil have effectively come to a halt since September last year following the expiry of a waiver which had been in place since the introduction of new Brazilian entry requirements in January 1996.
The problem centers around the tilletia controversa kuhn or TCK fungus which has been found in very limited areas in northern U.S. states.
In theory wheat from five U.S. states can still be exported to Brazil even under the new regulations but the U.S. system cannot guarantee the origin of wheat, officials have said.
Brazil's Wheat Industries Association has recently asked the government to consider ways to facilitate U.S. imports.
But at the meeting last week in Brasilia, officials from the two countries only discussed problems with fresh fruit, the Brazilian official said.
The wheat issue will be examined however at the North Carolina meeting on tilletias to be held on August 17-21 and which will be attended by four technicians from Brazil.
"It's possible that something could happen after this meeting," the official said.
